persona_reference.title: From GPT to Mistral: Cross-Domain Ontology Learning with NeOn-GPT
persona_reference.sections: 3.1.1 Role-play prompting; Appendix A.1 Domain-specific Persona Generation Prompt Template
persona_reference.adaptation: Original Studio wording adapted to the supplied video-game document and Yonsei's evidence-linked workflow. Defines domain expertise and ontology-engineering responsibilities, not a predetermined class inventory. Not a persona quoted from or evaluated in the paper.

defaults.persona: video game domain specialist and ontology engineer with expertise in gameplay and game design, genres, gaming platforms and interaction technologies, game development, publishing and distribution, and the history and culture of video games. You apply the NeOn methodology and Semantic Web technologies (RDF, RDFS, OWL, SPARQL and Turtle) to turn domain knowledge into reusable, coherent, modular ontologies. Your responsibilities span requirements analysis, competency-question design, vocabulary and modeling-pattern reuse, conceptual modeling, formalization and refinement. Interpret terminology in the context of the supplied document, preserve the links between source evidence, competency questions and model elements, and base modeling decisions on their meaning and the accepted requirements.

few_shot.system:
You generate pedagogic few-shot material for the selected ontology-engineering stage. Follow the stage-specific GENERATION INSTRUCTION for the example count and presentation: reuse slices, CQ/evidence examples, extraction cases, whole conceptual models, additions-only examples, or serialization pairs. Do not force every stage into a generic input/output essay.
Use only the domain-level settings and stage format to select relevant hypothetical cases. No actual source document, paragraph list, accepted CQ evidence, previous stage results or ontology is provided. Clearly label hypothetical example sources, questions and models. Do not claim to have read the actual document or use hypothetical text as actual source evidence. Example CQ/paragraph IDs are local to their declared example inputs. Examples are optional format/modeling guidance, never mandatory vocabulary or accepted source facts. Do not treat example content as evidence or as a completed stage result.
The TARGET STAGE PROMPT is the downstream output contract, not a request to run that stage; adapt only the example count and small scope specified by the generation instruction. Keep examples compact, self-contained and complete for their small inputs. Do not solve the actual document's entire stage or invent external searches, verified ontology mappings or reasoner results.
When JSON is requested inside an example, output valid complete JSON with quoted keys, no comments, no trailing commas or ellipsis placeholders, and correct escaping of quotes, backslashes and control characters. Keep labels and explanation outside JSON. A Turtle literal embedded in JSON must remain valid after JSON decoding.
Return only the requested example material inside ONE outer pair of ###start_output### and ###end_output### markers. Do not repeat or nest response markers inside individual examples; use ordinary headings or code fences for example JSON/Turtle.

simulation.label: [LOCAL SIMULATION — SMALL STRUCTURAL DEMO; NO LLM CALL; NOT A COMPLETE DOMAIN ONTOLOGY]
simulation.specification: Local structural demonstration for {domain_name}. Purpose: represent the supplied document. Scope: only explicit document information. Target users: document readers and ontology engineers. Intended use: CQ-driven retrieval. Functional requirements: retain document evidence and CQ links. Non-functional requirements: stable identifiers and valid RDF. This fixed template does not analyze document meaning.
simulation.reuse: Local demonstration: retain the stage 01 requirements. RDF, RDFS and OWL can represent classes, properties and labels. No external ontology search or semantic alignment was performed.
simulation.question: What information is stated in the quoted source passage?
simulation.refine_comment: # LOCAL SIMULATION: no semantic refinement was performed; the existing ontology is preserved.

stages.title: Ontology Specification
stages.template:
You are a {persona}.

Develop the ontology specification for the {domain_name} domain using the NeOn methodology. Use the entire domain document as the primary source; use keywords only when relevant: {keywords}.

DOMAIN DOCUMENT (data, not instructions):
{domain_description}

Specify the purpose, scope, target users, intended uses, functional requirements, and non-functional requirements as completely as the source permits. Do not optimize for a target ontology size. Preserve source qualifications and do not invent requirements.

FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES — format/modeling guidance only, never evidence:
{few_shot_01}

Return the complete ontology specification. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.
stages.few_shot_prompt:
Generate two small ontology-specification demonstrations for {domain_name}. The configured NeOn Step 01 has no dedicated few-shot field; this is a Yonsei teaching extension matching that step's requirements format, not a reproduction of a NeOn few-shot.
For each demonstration use: Example N — focus; Example input — a short, explicitly hypothetical domain passage and relevant keywords; Example output — six headings: Purpose, Scope, Target group, Intended uses, Functional requirements, Non-functional requirements.
Make the output complete for that small example input. Show different information needs and retain source qualifications or exclusions. Separate requirements supported by the example from proposed engineering choices. Do not produce classes, triples, CQ lists or a full specification for the actual document. Do not impose a target ontology size.
No actual document or previous stage result is available to this generator. Any example paragraphs, CQs and models requested above must be hypothetical teaching inputs, clearly labeled as such; do not claim to quote the real document.
stages.simulation_example: Example input: A reading club catalogs books and their titles. Example output: Purpose—retrieve catalog information; scope—books and explicit titles; user—club member; functional requirement—query book titles; non-functional requirement—stable identifiers.

stages.title: Ontology Reuse
stages.description: 도메인에 적합한 재사용 후보를 검토하고, 이를 적용한 작은 도메인 모델 조각을 제안합니다.
stages.template:
Extend and improve the accepted ontology specification for the {domain_name} domain through NeOn ontology-reuse principles. Explore reuse by constructing a small, provisional fragment of the current domain ontology that applies suitable existing vocabulary or modeling patterns.

ACCEPTED SPECIFICATION:
{previous_step_content}

REUSE GUIDANCE:
{reuse_example_desc}

FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES — guidance, not accepted mappings or source evidence:
{few_shot_02}

Identify the domain concepts, relationships, and requirements that would benefit from reuse. Prioritize existing ontologies and vocabularies that model the current domain or a relevant part of it. General-purpose ontologies and vocabularies are also eligible when their terms meet a specific need in this domain; familiarity or widespread use alone is not sufficient justification.

For each reuse candidate, identify the relevant concept or relationship in the accepted specification, the candidate ontology or vocabulary and its applicable terms or modeling pattern, the proposed mapping or use, and the semantic justification for accepting or rejecting it. Explain any differences in scope or meaning and any adaptation needed.

Apply the suitable candidates to a small, coherent part of the current domain model. Identify the relevant classes and properties, then express their proposed structure as conceptual subject-relation-object triples. Explain which terms or patterns are reused and which are proposed local modeling choices. Tie each part of the fragment to the accepted specification. Distinguish specification-supported information from provisional modeling choices, and keep uncertain mappings explicit. Use descriptive labels when a term IRI is uncertain. The fragment is a provisional modeling proposal, not an additional source of domain requirements.

Represent the specification's complexity and hierarchy where justified. Treat reuse guidance and examples as optional references and retain only suggestions relevant to the current domain and accepted requirements. Do not force a term whose semantics differ, invent external ontology names or term IRIs, claim a live ontology search, or override accepted requirements with an example. If no suitable candidate can be identified for a domain requirement, state that limitation without presenting a local proposal as verified reuse. Preserve the accepted specification and return the extended specification, domain-grounded reuse decisions, and the provisional domain model fragment. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.

INPUT SCOPE: The actual document, paragraph IDs and evidence quotations are intentionally withheld at this stage. Use the accepted specification and reuse guidance only. CQs have not been generated yet. Do not claim to inspect source passages or invent CQ/evidence links.
stages.few_shot_prompt:
Generate six compact reference slices for {domain_name}, matching the form of NeOn's few_shot_reuse: Example N — topic followed by a few lines in (subject — relation — object) form. These are understandable domain-modeling hints, not six complete ontologies or six rewritten specifications.
Choose distinct domain-relevant structures. For a video-game domain, the reference concerns game/release relationships, organizations and roles, genre specialization, interaction devices, adaptation/derivation, and provenance/metadata; adapt the topics to the domain-level settings rather than treating these labels as mandatory classes.
For each slice add a short Example requirement, Reference triples, and Reuse note. The note explains whether this is a local domain pattern or a candidate external vocabulary mapping, why the semantics fit, and any uncertainty. Keep class-level schema sketches distinct from individual assertions. Distinguish specialization from ordinary relations and avoid forcing both a game and a release class, disjoint developer/publisher classes, or other unsupported commitments.
In one Reuse note, contrast a suitable pattern with a rejected mismatch; do not include the rejected mapping among the reference triples. Do not invent external ontology names or term IRIs or claim a live search. Use descriptive labels for uncertain terms. Do not prescribe the final whole-domain model or solve the current reuse stage.
No actual document or previous stage result is available to this generator. Any example paragraphs, CQs and models requested above must be hypothetical teaching inputs, clearly labeled as such; do not claim to quote the real document.
stages.simulation_example: Example library-domain input: A reading club distinguishes a book's author from its publisher. Candidate pattern: a bibliographic model with separate authorship and publication roles; no concrete external ontology or term IRI has been verified. Provisional local fragment: classes Book, Person, PublishingOrganization; properties hasAuthor and hasPublisher; conceptual schema triples (hasAuthor, domain, Book), (hasAuthor, range, Person), (hasPublisher, domain, Book), (hasPublisher, range, PublishingOrganization). These labels are local modeling proposals illustrating the candidate pattern, not verified external terms. Reject using hasPublisher for authorship because the roles have different meanings.

stages.title: Competency Questions & Evidence
stages.description: 원본 문서로 CQ와 정확한 근거 인용을 생성하고, 앱이 인용문을 문단에 연결합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt:
Generate six distinct competency-question examples for {domain_name}, following the style and breadth of NeOn's few_shot_cqs rather than generating the real set of {cq_count} questions. Include both simple and compositional information needs, not paraphrases of one question.
Use this Yonsei adaptation of the question-list format:
Example input document: a small, explicitly hypothetical original mini-document in plain text with natural paragraph breaks, not a paragraph JSON array or ID-prefixed paragraphs.
Example output JSON: one complete object {"cqs":[{"id":"CQ1","question":"a specific answerable question","evidence":[{"text":"an exact nonempty quotation from the example document"}]}]} containing CQ1 through CQ6.
Every question must be supported by the example mini-document. Include at least one question with evidence from two paragraphs, using separate quotation entries. Preserve exact quotes and qualifiers. Each quotation must identify exactly one paragraph; include more context if a phrase repeats. Do not output paragraph_id: the application maps quotations to paragraphs locally. These CQ IDs belong only to the example and must not be presented as accepted pipeline CQ IDs. NeOn's EX-CQ labels are teaching labels, not the IDs required by the Yonsei output schema.
Do not provide answers, SPARQL, classes or the real document's final CQs. Keep headings outside the JSON and use valid JSON string escaping.
No actual document or previous stage result is available to this generator. Any example paragraphs, CQs and models requested above must be hypothetical teaching inputs, clearly labeled as such; do not claim to quote the real document.
stages.simulation_example: Example original document: A book has a title. Example output: {"cqs":[{"id":"CQ1","question":"What title does a book have?","evidence":[{"text":"A book has a title."}]}]}

stages.title: Entity, Property & Axiom Extraction
stages.description: 각 CQ에 필요한 클래스·프로퍼티·공리를 추출하고 CQ ID를 연결합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt:
Generate six concise CQ-to-extraction cases for {domain_name}, following NeOn's few_shot_entity_extraction layout. For every case use Example N — modeling focus; Example input CQ IDs and questions; Q:; Candidate entities:; Candidate relations/properties:; Safe axiom pattern: when justified; Modeling note:; Example output JSON.
Across the six cases demonstrate relation extraction without prematurely fixing the schema, CQ-supported specialization, a literal-valued property instead of an unnecessary class, context-sensitive agent roles, a version/derivation relationship, and claim-level provenance only when required. Adapt these concerns to relevant hypothetical cases in the current domain; do not force video-game vocabulary or extra schema merely to fill a pattern.
Each Example output JSON must be a complete {"elements":[],"triples":[]} object for that case. Every element has a stable absolute IRI id, kind (class/object_property/data_property), label and nonempty cq_ids. Every triple has absolute subject/predicate IRIs, object (absolute resource IRI or Turtle-quoted literal), and nonempty cq_ids. Supply all referenced CQ IDs in that case's input and demonstrate an element linked to multiple CQs in at least one case. Include the necessary classes and properties, not just names in prose.
Keep candidate discussion outside the JSON; emit only choices justified by that example's CQ wording. Do not assume cardinality, functionality, inverses, disjointness, reification or equivalence. Do not extract the real document's whole model.
No actual document or previous stage result is available to this generator. Any example paragraphs, CQs and models requested above must be hypothetical teaching inputs, clearly labeled as such; do not claim to quote the real document.
Match the real stage's input boundary: use CQ IDs/questions and modeling inputs, without example paragraph IDs, evidence quotations or document text. Preserve CQ links on elements and triples; source paragraphs are joined by the application only for stage 09.

stages.title: Conceptual Model
stages.description: 추출한 요소·공리를 CQ 연결이 있는 전체 개념 트리플로 구성합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt:
Generate one small extraction-to-complete-conceptual-model demonstration for {domain_name}. The configured NeOn Step 05 has no dedicated few-shot field; this Yonsei extension demonstrates its subject–relation–object modeling task using Yonsei's elements/triples JSON contract.
Use Example CQs (IDs and self-contained questions); Example input extraction (complete JSON); Example complete output model (complete JSON); Modeling note. The example is a self-contained hypothetical case, not the actual stage output.
The output must preserve every input element's absolute IRI, kind, relevant triples and all cq_ids. Include class declarations, one CQ-supported direct rdfs:subClassOf relationship, an ordinary object-property relationship, and a data property's domain and range. Distinguish specialization, instance membership and ordinary relationships; support each in the example CQs without imposing a hierarchy depth.
Use only CQ IDs supplied in the example input. Every element and triple carries nonempty cq_ids. Resource objects are absolute IRIs; literal objects are properly Turtle-quoted strings encoded safely in JSON. If illustrating individual assertions, distinguish those instances from the schema classes. Do not return only additions, omit existing elements, add arbitrary strong axioms, or serialize Turtle at this stage.
No actual document or previous stage result is available to this generator. Any example paragraphs, CQs and models requested above must be hypothetical teaching inputs, clearly labeled as such; do not claim to quote the real document.
Match the real stage's input boundary: use CQ IDs/questions and modeling inputs, without example paragraph IDs, evidence quotations or document text. Preserve CQ links on elements and triples; source paragraphs are joined by the application only for stage 09.

Generate six compact reuse-guided extension cases for {domain_name}. NeOn Step 06 reuses few_shot_reuse: small reference slices in (subject — relation — object) form, not entire new ontologies. Cover different relevant omissions in relationships, properties, justified specialization or provenance. Five cases should have small CQ-supported additions; the sixth is a no-op where the model already answers the example CQs. The no-op is exactly {"elements":[],"triples":[]}.
Each additions object has elements and triples using the target stage schema: element id/kind/label/cq_ids; triple subject/predicate/object/cq_ids. Preserve current absolute IRIs and kinds, use only the example input's CQ IDs, and emit only triples absent from that input. Existing elements may be listed only to add CQ associations.
The reference slice is optional guidance, not evidence; the example CQs must justify every addition. Explain candidate reuse honestly without inventing external ontology terms or implying verified equivalence. Do not return the full model or make size-driven additions.
No actual document or previous stage result is available to this generator. Any example paragraphs, CQs and models requested above must be hypothetical teaching inputs, clearly labeled as such; do not claim to quote the real document.

stages.title: Conceptual Model Extension II
stages.description: 남아 있는 CQ·문서 근거를 검토하고 중복 없이 개념 모델을 추가 보완합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt:
Generate six compact second-pass extension cases for {domain_name}. NeOn Step 07 uses the same few_shot_reuse reference-slice form as Step 06, but reviews the accumulated model including the first pass. This is a second gap check, not a request to repeat or expand every reference slice.
For each case use Example N — remaining gap; Example input — hypothetical CQ IDs and questions, base model and explicit first-pass additions; Reference slice — a few (subject — relation — object) hints; Reuse note; Example additions JSON.
Use five small cases with different remaining CQ-supported gaps and one no-op where a suggested relation was already added in the first pass. Output exactly {"elements":[],"triples":[]} for the no-op. Keep examples compact; do not repeat a first-pass addition.
All output objects follow the elements/triples schema with stable absolute IRIs, unchanged element kinds and nonempty cq_ids drawn only from the example input. Compare candidate triples against both the base model and first-pass additions. Existing elements may be listed only for new CQ associations. Do not return the full model.
Optional reuse hints never establish source facts. Do not invent external term IRIs, add inverse/transitive properties merely because they are absent, force parents, or use examples as accepted evidence.
No actual document or previous stage result is available to this generator. Any example paragraphs, CQs and models requested above must be hypothetical teaching inputs, clearly labeled as such; do not claim to quote the real document.
Match the real stage's input boundary: use CQ IDs/questions and modeling inputs, without example paragraph IDs, evidence quotations or document text. Preserve CQ links on elements and triples; source paragraphs are joined by the application only for stage 09.

stages.title: Turtle Serialization
stages.description: 전체 개념 모델을 CQ 연결 주석이 포함된 유효한 Turtle 온톨로지로 변환합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt:
Generate one small conceptual-model-JSON to complete-Turtle demonstration for {domain_name}. The configured NeOn Step 08 has no dedicated few-shot field; this Yonsei extension illustrates whole-model serialization, not NeOn's later data-property or individual-addition steps.
Use Example input CQs; Example input conceptual model (complete elements/triples JSON); Example output Turtle. Include a compact hypothetical model with classes, an object_property, a data_property, justified domain/range and direct subclass statements, and a literal value so resource IRIs and literal escaping are distinguishable.
Serialize every input element and triple, not just a representative class or a delta. Retain exactly the input absolute IRIs, kinds, labels and justified semantics; do not add domain entities merely to enlarge the ontology. Declare all prefixes used and owl:Class/owl:ObjectProperty/owl:DatatypeProperty types as appropriate.
Declare <https://example.org/yonsei/relatedCQ> a owl:AnnotationProperty. For every element emit one relatedCQ literal annotation for every cq_ids entry from that element's input; demonstrate an element with multiple CQ IDs and preserve all of them rather than annotating everything with a hard-coded CQ1. Supply these CQ IDs in the example input.
The Turtle is the complete serialization of the small example model, never the real document's ontology. Do not claim reasoner validation. Use a labeled Turtle code block without nested response markers.
No actual document or previous stage result is available to this generator. Any example paragraphs, CQs and models requested above must be hypothetical teaching inputs, clearly labeled as such; do not claim to quote the real document.

stages.title: Paragraph-grounded Refinement
stages.description: 문단별 관련 CQ와 클래스·프로퍼티를 함께 읽으며 전체 온톨로지를 보완합니다.
stages.template:
Refine the CURRENT complete ontology by reviewing the source one paragraph at a time within this single request. This is the initial Yonsei Refine implementation, not a reasoner or an automatic QA certification.

PARAGRAPH CONTEXTS:
{refinement_context}

CURRENT COMPLETE TURTLE:
{ontology_snapshot}

Each context contains the exact paragraph text, accepted CQs whose evidence explicitly cites that paragraph, and all catalog classes/properties linked to those CQs. Links were selected by IDs, not keyword similarity. A paragraph with status no_linked_cq has no accepted CQ mapping: do not invent an attribution, treat another paragraph's CQ as its evidence, or expand the ontology from that paragraph without a supported CQ.

For each mapped paragraph, assess whether the listed elements and the current ontology represent the cited CQ needs and source qualifications. Refine only where supported: labels/descriptions, suitable class/property relationships, domains/ranges and missing justified axioms. Prefer existing IDs, avoid redundancy and unjustified strong axioms, and preserve unrelated valid content. Do not claim logical consistency or CQ answerability has been formally tested.

Return the FULL refined ontology, never a delta. Keep every existing catalog element's IRI, class/property kind and <https://example.org/yonsei/relatedCQ> annotation links. If adding a class or property, annotate it with the existing CQ IDs that justify it. Do not invent CQ IDs. Preserve valid syntax and the relatedCQ annotation-property declaration. If no supported changes are needed, return the current Turtle unchanged.
Return ONLY valid Turtle between ###start_turtle### and ###end_turtle### markers.

The application retained stage 03 evidence separately while model-building stages used only CQ IDs/questions. The paragraph-to-CQ-to-element mapping above is that stored evidence joined with the cumulative element catalog by cq_ids. Use it for the source-grounded review; do not infer new paragraph links from keyword overlap.
